How to stop QuickBooks invoice reminders for one customer

In most QuickBooks Online plans you cannot leave one customer out of automatic reminders. On Advanced you can. Here are your options, and how to turn them off.

Checked 2026-11-21. Menus in other products change, so a label may differ slightly on your screen.

Short answer: in QuickBooks Online, automatic invoice reminders apply to the whole company. Intuit's help says you cannot turn them off for a single customer or invoice. To stop them, go to Settings, then Account and settings, then Sales, and turn off Automatic invoice reminders for everyone. Then send reminders by hand to the customers who need one. On QuickBooks Online Advanced, you can leave a customer out by using a reminder workflow whose customer condition lists only the customers who should get reminders.

If a good customer got a reminder

This is common. A reminder goes out to a customer who already agreed a later payment date, who is on a payment plan, or who you simply do not want to nag. It is a setting, not a mistake on your part. A short apology usually settles it, and the template further down can help.

What the standard reminders can and cannot do

In Simple Start, Essentials and Plus, automatic reminders are one switch for the whole company. You can choose how many days before or after the due date each reminder goes out, and add up to three. You cannot pick customers, and you cannot skip one invoice. Intuit's own help says so, and so do Intuit staff in the community forum.

Option 1: turn reminders off and remind by hand

This is the method Intuit points to.

  1. Select the gear icon for Settings, then Account and settings, then the Sales tab.
  2. In the Reminders section, select the pencil (edit) icon.
  3. Turn off Automatic invoice reminders, then save and close.

Your wording and timing are kept, so you can turn reminders back on later without starting over.

To remind a customer yourself, go to Invoices, find the invoice, and in the Action column choose Send reminder. Change the message if you like, then select Send. You pick who gets one, so the good customer is left alone.

The cost is that you must remember to do it. A simple weekly look at your overdue invoices is enough. Our guide on chasing overdue invoices by email has wording you can use.

Option 2: do not email that one invoice from QuickBooks

Intuit says reminders only go to invoices you have already emailed. If you keep one customer's invoice from being emailed through QuickBooks, for example by downloading the PDF and sending it yourself, the automatic reminder has nothing to attach to. Intuit does not describe this as a way to leave a customer out, so test it on one invoice first. The price is that you give up sending that customer's invoices from QuickBooks.

Option 3: QuickBooks Online Advanced workflows

QuickBooks Online Advanced is the top plan. On it, the answer is yes. Intuit's help says you can use workflows to create invoice reminders, and a reminder workflow has a customer condition. The customer is either "within All" or you select specific customers.

  1. Select the gear icon for Settings, then Manage workflows.
  2. Start a reminder from Templates, or open My workflows, find your invoice reminder and choose Edit in the Actions column.
  3. In the customer condition, pick the customers who should get reminders from the customer drop-down. Leave out the one you want to skip.
  4. Select Save and turn on (some screens say Save and enable).

Menu names vary a little, so check your screen.

There is a catch. The list names who is included, not who is left out. A new customer gets no reminders until you add them to the list. Check it now and then.

If emails keep coming after you turn off the standard setting, check My workflows too.

How to turn reminders off completely

  1. Turn off Automatic invoice reminders under Settings, then Account and settings, then Sales, then Reminders.
  2. If you have Advanced, go to Settings, then Manage workflows, then My workflows. Find any invoice reminder workflow, choose Disable and confirm.
  3. Look at your recurring invoice templates (Settings, then Recurring transactions). Intuit lists templates set to send automatically as another source of emails.

When an invoice is already paid

Reminders go to invoices that are still unpaid. Once an invoice is marked paid, it stops matching the reminder rules. The usual cause of a reminder on a paid invoice is a payment that was received but never recorded against that invoice. Record the payment now and open the invoice to check that it shows Paid.

If a customer got a reminder on an invoice that does show Paid, turn off the automatic setting and contact QuickBooks support.

Smoothing things over with the customer

Keep it short and warm. Do not explain the software.

Subject: Please ignore our reminder Hi [name], You may have received an automatic reminder about invoice [invoice number] for [amount]. Please ignore it. [We have agreed a payment date of [due date].] [Your account is up to date.] Sorry for the bother. If anything about the invoice is unclear, just reply and we will sort it out. Thank you, [your name]

If the customer is on a payment plan or has an agreement with you, the reminder may also have been confusing for them. Say so plainly in your note. Late fees and what you may charge depend on your agreement with the customer and your state's law. This is not legal advice.

Where this leaves you

You have three choices: reminders for everyone, reminders by hand, or, on QuickBooks Online Advanced, a reminder workflow that lists the customers who should get them. If you are not on Advanced and want automatic reminders that skip certain customers, you need a tool that keeps a list of people to leave alone. Also see how to automate invoice reminders in QuickBooks Online and how often to send invoice reminders.
